title: The Wall Between Our Gardens
thread: Her silent 81-year-old neighbour leaves something on the dry-stone wall every week; she has never known how to thank him, so she cooks him lunch from the garden and leaves it on the wall.
funny: the cat claims the harvest basket; the crumble burns on one side, so 'the good side faces out, that's called presentation'
turn: next morning the basket is back, washed, with a note: 'Bit salty. Same time next week?'

title: Grandma's Bean Row
thread: She plants runner beans from a paper envelope of seeds her grandmother saved and labelled in pencil the year before she died; today is the first picking.
funny: the beans grew far past the canes and she needs a kitchen chair to reach them; the dog eats the one bean she drops
turn: she finds a second envelope in the tin, labelled 'for next year, love'
close: She saves a handful of seeds and writes a new envelope.

title: The Jam That Never Set
thread: Every summer she tries her mother's apricot jam and every summer it stays runny; today she makes it again, and calls her mother while it cooks.
funny: the jam doesn't set again; she pours it over yoghurt and calls it 'apricot sauce, on purpose'
turn: her mother laughs and admits hers never set either; she just never told anyone
close: Some recipes are just an excuse to call home.

title: One Tomato
thread: Her first year growing tomatoes: forty plants, one stubborn green tomato that won't turn red, and a lesson about waiting.
funny: she talks to the tomato every morning; a blackbird eats it the day it finally turns red
turn: the other thirty-nine plants all ripen at once and she has to give tomatoes to the whole village
close: I wanted one perfect tomato. I got a village full of friends.

title: The Pear Tree That Rests
thread: The old pear tree gives fruit only every second year; this is the good year, and she thinks about the year she rested too.
funny: a pear lands on the cat's tail; the cat refuses to forgive the tree all day
turn: a jar of poached pears goes to the friend who told her it was okay to rest
close: Even trees take a year off.

title: Snow Peas for Mr. Okada
thread: She learns to grow snow peas from the retired farmer down the lane who corrects her by moving her canes when she isn't looking.
funny: every morning one cane has moved; she finally catches him at it
turn: she brings him the first bowl of pea rice; he says it needs more salt and eats two bowls
close: Some teachers never say they're teaching.

title: The Lemon on the Windowsill
thread: A lemon tree in a pot that came with the house, and a note in the drawer from the woman who lived there before: 'water it on Sundays'.
funny: she waters it every day for a week; the tree drops leaves in protest; Sundays it is
turn: she leaves her own note in the drawer for whoever comes next
close: Water it on Sundays. And bake something with the lemons.

title: Bread for a Rainy Day
thread: On a rainy day she bakes the soda bread her dad made every Saturday, and finally understands why he always made two loaves.
funny: the first loaf is a doorstop; the dog carries it into the garden and buries it
turn: the second loaf goes, still warm, to the woman at the end of the lane who lives alone

title: The Hens Who Wouldn't
thread: Three new hens and not one egg in three weeks; she stops checking, starts just sitting with them in the morning.
funny: she gives the hens a pep talk; they ignore it completely
turn: the morning she forgets to look, there are three eggs in the flower pot, not the nest box
close: Good things come when you stop staring at them.

title: Soup for the Builder
thread: A quiet builder is fixing the old stone wall in the cold; every day at noon she wonders whether to bring him something warm.
funny: she makes the soup three days in a row and eats it herself each time
turn: on the fourth day she brings it; he has brought her a flask of tea for the same reason
close: Bring the soup on the first day.

title: Plum Season
thread: Plum dumplings were the one thing her grandfather cooked; she makes them for the first time, from his handwriting.
funny: the recipe says 'enough flour'; she uses far too much, then far too little
turn: the last dumpling holds together, and it tastes exactly right
close: Enough flour is however much it takes.

title: The Sunflower Bet
thread: Her little brother bet her in spring that his sunflower would grow taller than hers; he moved to the city, and she has measured both every week since.
funny: his sunflower wins by a hand; she tries standing on tiptoe to measure
turn: she sends him a photo and the loser's peach tart by post, badly packed

title: Kimchi and the First Frost
thread: Before the first frost she makes kimchi alone for the first time, the day her mother used to call the neighbours to help.
funny: she makes enough for a whole village because she used her mother's quantities
turn: she knocks on doors with jars; by evening the neighbours are in her kitchen
close: Kimchi was never meant to be made alone.

title: The Courgette Problem
thread: She planted six courgette plants. Nobody warned her. A quietly funny day of trying to use them all.
funny: courgettes appear faster than she can cook them; she leaves one on every doorstep in the lane
turn: the next morning there are courgettes on her doorstep: everyone had the same idea

title: Teacups for Two
place: Kyoto machiya with a small courtyard garden
thread: She still sets out two teacups out of habit after her flatmate moved away; today the second cup gets a new guest.
funny: the second cup is claimed by the neighbour's cat, who drinks from it
turn: the flatmate calls at the exact moment she finally puts the second cup away

title: A Garden for Someone Else
thread: She plants a small bed of strawberries for her elderly neighbour, who can't kneel any more, and harvests them for her.
funny: the neighbour gives detailed critiques of every strawberry
turn: the neighbour teaches her the shortcake she made for her late husband
close: Plant something you won't eat yourself.
